focus: Q4: costs and risks of restore vs new checker vs keep closed
noveltyJustification: Priced the three paths against measured size, dependency and CI facts; refined the frozen-table inventory to eight locations with lockstep tests covering only some; identified that no standing gate compares compiled to legacy since retirement.
answeredQuestions: KQ-4 (complete: costs/risks per path with sources)

ruledOut.reason: Out of scope by the spec fence and far larger; the archived manual sweep shows modules can be driven without the lane

finding: Eight live cohort copies/registries: HUB_CHILD, runtime resolver, authored resolver, advisor flag source, advisor dist, guard HUBS, sync HUBS, serving-closure hubs[]; lockstep tests cover resolver and advisor families and HUB_CHILD<->advisor, but not guard/sync/closure.

Modules-only restore = 4,241 lines + test + driver; verbatim today only thanks to migration symlinks; post-migration path edits force re-pinning the frozen trio; full lane restore is strictly larger and out of scope.
Buys the only two-observation compiled-vs-legacy verdict with anti-tamper pins; risks re-opening a deliberately retired lane with no owning command, deleted docs, and workspace coupling.

A new checker needs a frontmatter gold reader, the live qualifiedIdToLeaf bridge, scoring incl. defer/UNKNOWN/negative/holdout partition, and a report - low hundreds of lines, no frozen parts; a partial CI precedent exists (golden-prompt joined-mode, 2 fixtures).
One observation not two: bar shifts to gold agreement; checker owns the oracle; corpus floors required; admission machinery unchanged regardless.

Zero build; retains a documented blocked path and permanent manual admission; no standing gate compares compiled to legacy since retirement (freshness only proves inputs->manifest); cohort shrinks (7->6->5) with no low-friction path in.
